sakka.notes: Sakka 03 belongs with the Sakyan clan. DPD has sakka 3 and sakkā 2 for this use, but neither is a packet sense. AN 11.13 calls Nandiya a Sakyan (sakko). The English name filter misses that use, and none of the Sakka 03 placements in AN 8.14–16 supplies it. Two texts need different entries at different taps. DN 20:1.2 and 2.2 locate the assembly among the Sakyans (sakkesu), and 14.10 names the god Purindada. Thag 21.1:57.1 addresses the Buddha as a Sakyan (sakka), and 58.4 compares him to the thousand-eyed god. The parallel Snp 2.12:4.1 uses the distinct form sakya for the Buddha. SN 10.2 calls its speaker a yakkha named Sakka and gives no royal epithet. MN 56:29.37 applies the divine titles to the Buddha. MN 98:13.16 and Snp 3.9:68.4 apply Brahmā and Sakka to one who has ended rebirth. SN 40.11 refers back to the Sakka discourse in its repetition instruction and closing list. Two clear mentions missing through verse alignment are Snp 3.11:1.2 and Thig 7.1:7.1. The entry gives Sunetta thirty-five births as Sakka, while AN 7.66:13.6 says thirty-six. The SN 2 page includes Maghada and Dāmali in 2.4–5 alongside Māgha in 2.3. SN 9.7–9 and SN 40.9 also concern other subjects.

sakuludāyī.notes: The two conversations at the peacocks’ feeding ground are MN 77 and MN 79. AN 4.30 and AN 4.185 name Sakuludāyī with Annabhāra and Varadhara on the riverbank. The page placement also picks up AN 4.28–29.

sakulā.notes: Thig 5.7 names the nun and recounts her development of clairvoyance. AN 1.242 gives the same distinction to bakulā in the local Pali and Sakulā in Sujato, explaining the missing packet mention. The other two AN page placements fall outside the nuns’ list. In MN 90 the sisters Somā and Sakulā send greetings through Pasenadi. The sutta establishes the episode but leaves their marital status unstated. The placement in MN 89 is on the preceding discourse.

salalāgāra.notes: SN 52.8 opens at Anuruddha’s salaḷa tree hut. SN 52.7 gives only Sāvatthī. The chapter summary at SN 52.10:3.3 repeats the hut’s name. DN 21:1.9.5 uses the separately glossed diminutive salaḷāgārake for the hut in Sakka’s account.

sambara.notes: SN 11.10 names the titan lord the seers approach for safety. In SN 11.23 Vepacitti speaks of Sambara in the third person. The proposed identification with Vepacitti comes from the commentary. SN 11.9 and SN 11.24 are neighboring page placements.

sambhūta.notes: DPD assigns verses 291–294 to this sense, and Thag 4.7:4.5 names their speaker Sambhūta. The untranslated chapter summary at Thag 4.12:5.4 also names him. The candidate explicitly describes the elder of verse 6. Thag 1.6 names him Sītavaniya and describes his meditation in the Cool Wood. His entry belongs in others, leaving the Thag 4.7 elder without a matching candidate.

samiddhi.notes: Thag 1.46 attributes the verse with the joined form Samiddhitthero. MN 133 places the monk at the hot springs. Sāriputta questions him in AN 9.14, while the adjacent AN 9.13 addresses Mahākoṭṭhita. The AN 9.20 hit is a chapter summary. The untranslated summaries at SN 4.25:26.1 and Thag 1.50:2.4 also name Samiddhi.

sanaṅkumāra.notes: SN 6.11 places Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra on the Sappinī and attributes the verse to him. SN 6.10 and 6.12 are neighboring discourses. DN 3:1.28.1 explicitly credits him with the verse, although the reference lands in DN 4. SN 21.11 gives the verse to the Buddha, as the entry says. Its neighboring placements SN 21.10 and 21.12 do not contain it.

sandhāna.notes: DN 25 names the Rājagaha householder in conversation with Nigrodha. The lay disciples’ list names him at AN 6.120–139:1.14. The page also picks up AN 6.119 on Tapussa and AN 6.140 on greed.

santusita.notes: AN 8.36:7.3 identifies the god by his standing among the Tusita gods. SN 40.11:3.1 names him. DN 11:75.1 spells the name santussito. The placements in AN 8.37 and SN 40.10 belong to adjacent discourses.

santuṭṭha.notes: DN 16 and SN 55.10 name Santuṭṭha among the deceased Ñātikā lay followers who had ended the five lower fetters. Both describe spontaneous rebirth and final extinguishment there. Only the entry specifies Akaniṭṭha. The SN 55.9 placement falls on an earlier list.

sappasoṇḍikapabbhāra.notes: DN 16 locates the grotto in the Cool Grove at Rājagaha. SN 35.69 opens there with Sāriputta and Upasena. The neighboring SN 35.68 is Samiddhi’s question about the world.

sarabha.notes: The three challenges to the former monk take place in AN 3.64 in this corpus. The page also lands in AN 3.63 at Venāgapura. DPD’s AN 3.65 is the Kesamutta discourse in this numbering. The untranslated chapter summary at AN 3.70:41.2 also names Sarabha.

sarabhaṅga.notes: MN 116 lists the independent Buddha. The elder explains his name by recounting how he broke reeds in Thag 7.5:1. Additional mentions in the verse body are sarabhaṅgoti at 1.3 and Sarabhaṅgo at 3.2. Sujato gives the name in English at 3.1.

sarabhū.notes: SN 13.3 and SN 13.4 list the Sarabhū among the five rivers that converge. The page placement also includes SN 13.5, whose comparison concerns the great earth.
